# Third-party license texts shipped in the kapi-av tarball

## `COPYING.LGPLv2.1`

The LGPL-2.1 text covering the ffmpeg and ffprobe binaries this plugin bundles.
LGPL-2.1 §1 requires a copy of the license to travel with the library, and the
`NOTICE` beside it is attribution rather than the grant.

**Do not edit this file.** It is FFmpeg's own copy, fetched verbatim from the
tag the release builds:

```bash
curl -sSfL -o plugins/av/licenses/COPYING.LGPLv2.1 \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/n7.1.4/COPYING.LGPLv2.1
```

That tag is `FFMPEG_SOURCE_TAG` in `.github/workflows/release-av.yml`. Taking
the text from FFmpeg rather than from a general LGPL source means it ships from
the project it covers. Retyping a license, or reconstructing one from memory, is
never acceptable: the text is the grant.

It was checked against the FSF's own copy
(`https://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/lgpl-2.1.txt`) when it was added.
The operative sections are identical. Three cosmetic differences remain, all of
them FSF editorial changes made after FFmpeg last synced its copy:

| line | FSF today | FFmpeg's copy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| header address | `<https://fsf.org/>` | the Franklin Street postal address |
| §16 "how to apply" | "see `<https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>`" | "write to the Free Software Foundation" |
| example signature | Moe Ghoul | Ty Coon |

Neither variant changes what the license permits or requires.

## Vendoring rather than fetching at release time

The alternative was to pull the text out of the FFmpeg distribution during the
release. That was rejected for two reasons. The macOS leg clones the source and
keeps only the two binaries, and BtbN's prebuilt archives do not document
whether they carry a license file at all, so the lookup would differ per leg and
break silently when an archive layout changed. A release should also not need
the network to stay compliant.

If `FFMPEG_SOURCE_TAG` moves to a version whose licensing differs, refresh this
file with the command above in the same commit that moves the tag.
